Common issues

My pipeline isn't processing events

Check the source connector's health field via the Connectors endpoint. A down connector stalls every pipeline that reads from it. If it's healthy, confirm the pipeline itself is active and not paused — see Scheduling & triggers.

Events keep failing and landing in the dead-letter queue

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

What happens when you exceed your quota

When your account reaches its quota limit, the API behaves differently depending on the type of limit that was exceeded:

Rate limit (requests per minute)

When you exceed your per-minute rate limit, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests status code. The response includes a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying. See Rate limit headers in the API reference for details on tracking your usage with response headers.

Action to take: Implement exponential backoff in your client to automatically retry failed requests after the delay specified in Retry-After. If you consistently hit the rate limit, consider upgrading your plan tier.

Daily quota exceeded

Once you exceed your daily request quota, all API requests return a 429 Too Many Requests status with a message indicating the daily quota was exceeded. Your quota resets at midnight UTC each day.

Action to take: Wait for the quota reset at midnight UTC, or upgrade to a higher plan tier with a larger daily quota. Contact support if you need a temporary quota increase.

Data retention limit exceeded

Event data older than your plan's retention period is automatically deleted and cannot be recovered. For example, Starter-tier accounts only retain 7 days of event history.

Action to take: If you need to keep historical event data longer, export it before the retention window expires, or upgrade to a plan tier with extended retention. Standard tier retains data for 30 days.

Monitor your usage

Check your workspace settings or billing dashboard regularly to monitor your API usage, remaining quota, and data retention status. Set up alerts in your monitoring system to notify you when you approach a quota limit.

Upgrading your plan

To upgrade from Starter to Standard, or to discuss custom limits for an Enterprise plan:

  1. Log in to your workspace at https://app.godzilladocs.dev
  2. Go to Settings → Billing
  3. Choose your new plan and complete the payment process

For Enterprise plans or custom quota requests, contact our sales team.

Frequently asked questions

Do I get charged for failed requests?

No. Requests that return an error (including 429 rate-limit responses) do not count against your quota or billing.

Can I get a temporary quota increase?

Yes. Contact support with details about your use case, and we can discuss a temporary increase or recommend the right plan tier for your needs.

What is the monthly billing cycle?

Billing cycles run from the 1st to the last day of each calendar month. Charges appear on the billing method on file shortly after the end of the cycle. For annual plans, billing runs on the anniversary of your purchase date.

Can I downgrade my plan?

Yes. You can downgrade anytime from your billing settings, and the change takes effect on your next billing cycle. Please note that downgrading may reduce your rate limits and data retention.

Migration guide (v2 → v3)

v3 of the pipelines endpoint ships with improved error handling, batch operations, and enhanced filtering. This guide covers breaking changes and new capabilities.

What's new in v3

  • Error handling policies — Configure retry, dead-letter queue (DLQ), or discard behavior per pipeline.
  • Batch operations — Create or update multiple pipelines in a single request.
  • Enhanced filtering — Filter pipelines by state, connector, or tags in list operations.
  • Improved error messages — More actionable error responses with suggested remediation.

Update your base URL

All v3 requests use the new base URL:

v2 → v3 diff 
- https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines
+ https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines

Breaking changes

v3 is backwards-compatible with v2 for basic create/list/delete operations. The following are the only breaking changes:

  • error_policy field is now required in pipeline responses (defaults to retry if not set).
  • List operations now include a total_count field for pagination context.

Add error handling policies

v3 introduces structured error handling. When creating or updating a pipeline, specify an error policy:

pipeline-with-error-handling.json json 
{\n  \"name\": \"ingest-orders\",\n  \"source_connector_id\": \"conn_pg_orders\",\n  \"destination_connector_id\": \"conn_snowflake_dw\",\n  \"error_handling\": {\n    \"policy\": \"retry\",\n    \"max_attempts\": 3,\n    \"backoff_ms\": 1000\n  }\n}

Supported policies:

  • retry — Retry failed events up to max_attempts times (default).
  • dlq — Write failed events to a dead-letter queue for later inspection.
  • discard — Silently drop failed events (use with caution).

Use batch operations

Migration guide (v1 → v2) v1 retired

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Rate limits & errors for the exact envelope.

diff diff 
- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20
+ GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

v1 is retired

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.
